object_context: Child of H4d1d. Fix a smooth projective complex family X->T on an irreducible reduced Hodge-locus branch for a fixed flat rational class alpha and an exact-category witness-incidence problem. Determine whether monodromy/component switching really requires one global witness section, or whether an exact-class witness family on a finite cover can be descended by rational proper pushforward/trace. Root initial algebraicity is outside this atom.

ambient fibres are smooth projective complex varieties and alpha is a fixed flat rational Hodge class
the witness category must remain algebraic cycles/Chow data of codimension p
domination of witness incidence does not by itself produce a global section or a finite multisection
a finite-cover trace is useful only if the upstairs cycle has exact class equal to the pullback of alpha
generic finite-flat descent, ramified/singular boundary specialization, completion descent, and root initial algebraicity are separate obligations
equivalent_formulations: replace a global witness section by a finite multisection/finite cover carrying exact-class witnesses
test whether degree-normalized proper pushforward descends a Q-cycle from a finite cover to the branch family
separate finite-cover existence, exact class identity, and singular-boundary gluing into independent atoms

invariant aggregate -> degree-normalized proper pushforward Q-cycle
preserved additive invariant -> exact target cycle class
